paper.title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
paper.abstract:
Objectives: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.
Methods: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context.
Results: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed.
Conclusions: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

paper.title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
paper.abstract: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites. The AI system adopted a two-level architecture: The first level used EfficientNet-B3 for rapid screening on x-ray films; the second level used 3D nnU-Net (No-new-Net) to segment intestinal wall gas, and then fused the data through a three-branch network (gas morphology, accompanying signs, and clinical metadata) via cross-attention to output the probability of ischemic PI. In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.947 for ischemic PI (sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 93.6%), significantly outperforming senior radiologists (AUC = 0.876); the AUC on the external validation set was 0.931. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that PVG and blood lactate were the most important predictors. This two-tiered AI system can significantly improve the early identification of the causes of critical PI, providing a reliable method for intelligent diagnosis of emergency imaging.

paper.title: Zaizao Shengxue capsule for anemia: a prospective multicenter real-world study of hemoglobin response and predictive modeling.
paper.abstract:
Objective: The aim in this study was to characterize the 8-week hemoglobin response among patients with anemia receiving Zaizao Shengxue capsule (ZSC) in real-world care and develop and externally evaluate a model for estimating the individual probability of response.
Methods: This prospective multicenter study included 440 patients from 14 centers who received ZSC for 8 weeks. Response was defined as an increase in hemoglobin of at least 20 g/L from baseline at week 8. The development cohort (n = 338) was divided into a training cohort (n = 238) and an internal validation cohort (n = 100). Baseline predictors were selected in the training cohort. Ten candidate models were trained using different algorithms and compared in the internal validation cohort. After model selection and locking, the final model was independently evaluated in 102 patients from four external centers. SHAP and LIME were used for model interpretation.
Results: Overall, 204 of 440 patients (46.4%) achieved an 8-week hemoglobin response. Response rates varied across anemia etiologies: 24.0% in cancer-related anemia (60/250), 74.4% in iron-deficiency anemia (67/90), and 77.0% in anemia of chronic disease (77/100). Anemia etiology, age, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were retained as predictors in the final Extra Trees model. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI, 0.729-0.902) in internal validation and 0.769 (95% CI, 0.670-0.860) in external validation. SHAP analysis identified anemia etiology as the largest contributor to model predictions, followed by age and eGFR.
Conclusion: Eight-week hemoglobin response varied across anemia etiologies among patients receiving ZSC. A model incorporating anemia etiology, age, and eGFR may support individualized pretreatment estimation of response probability based on routinely available clinical information.

paper.title: DeepFusion-HSK: a multimodal deep learning for subtype classification of herpes simplex keratitis with multicenter validation.
paper.abstract:
Introduction: To develop and evaluate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model for subtype classification of viral keratitis.
Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 3,501 slit-lamp images (807 eyes) as the internal development set and two external validation cohorts (2,957 images total). DeepFusion-HSK integrates three complementary illumination modalities-diffuse light imaging (DLI), slit-beam imaging (SBI), and fluorescein staining imaging (FSI)-through a novel fusion architecture. The framework uses a tri-way higher-order interaction layer to capture cross-modal pathological signatures, dual-task learning with auxiliary heads to prevent modality-specific feature degradation, and a dynamic gating mechanism that uses high-confidence coarse priors to calibrate fine-grained predictions and mitigate softmax probability spillover. To simulate real-world data deficiency, we evaluated model resilience under complete FSI dropout.
Results: On the internal test set, DeepFusion-HSK achieved an accuracy of 85.1% (95% CI: 78.5%-90.0%) and AUCs of 0.947-0.949 for discriminating epithelial herpes simplex keratitis (E-HSK) and non-epithelial herpes simplex keratitis (NE-HSK), significantly outperforming Swin-Transformer, EfficientNetV2, and ResNet50. External validation confirmed robust generalization, with accuracies of 81.7% on Dataset I and 78.2% on Dataset II, demonstrating clinical resilience. Ablation studies confirmed the hierarchical synergy of multimodal inputs: the best single modality (FSI) yielded 78.5% accuracy, the optimal dual-modality combination (DLI + FSI) reached 81.7%, and full tri-modal fusion improved performance to 85.1%, validating that integrated global morphology, depth contour, and superficial ulcer signatures are essential for robust HSK subtyping.
Discussion: DeepFusion-HSK offers a robust, generalizable, and clinically deployable solution for therapeutic HSK subtyping. Its resilience to missing imaging modalities makes it well suited for heterogeneous real-world ophthalmic practice, providing a decision-support tool to reduce vision-threatening misdiagnoses and guide therapy.

paper.title: An integrated CT/MRI diagnostic system for pancreatic cystic lesions that supports pathological classification and risk stratification.
paper.abstract:
Objective: To develop a pathology-based preoperative decision-support system (Structured Imaging Report System for Pancreatic Cystic Lesions, SIRS-PCL) for subtype classification and risk stratification of PCLs.
Methods: We conducted a multicentre retrospective study involving 1,102 patients treated between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2024. The study cohort was divided into a development dataset (n = 858) and a temporal validation dataset (n = 244) from the periods 2011-2022 and 2023-2024, respectively. Three logistic prediction models were used to classify the five PCL subtypes and to perform separate three-tier risk stratifications (benign/low, medium, and high) for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) and mucinous cystic neoplasm (MCN) cases. SIRS-PCL was prospectively implemented at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital from 25 June 2025 to 25 June 2026, and the diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were evaluated in a cohort of 76 patients.
Results: A total of 1,102 patients with PCLs were included in the study (median age 56 years, interquartile range 44-64), of whom 714 were female (64.8%). The five-category model included in SIRS-PCL achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.93 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.91-0.95] in temporal validation. The IPMN model showed good discrimination for risk stratification (mean AUC 0.86, 95% CI 0.79-0.93), with the highest overall accuracy of 77.1% exceeding current guidelines (range 50.0%-58.6%). The MCN risk model also showed high performance (mean AUC 0.97, 95% CI 0.91-1.00). In comparison to current practice, SIRS-PCL use reduced unnecessary surgeries 11.5% vs. 23.1% and over-examinations 6.7% vs 33.7%. In the prospective implementation cohort, SIRS-PCL achieved accuracy of 86.2% for five-category pathological classification, 73.7% for IPMN risk stratification, and 100% for MCN risk stratification.
Conclusions: SIRS-PCL is a pathology-based, quantitative decision-support system for preoperative pathological subtype classification and pathological risk stratification of surgically evaluated neoplastic PCLs.
